sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 那么这种转移话题的做法效果如何？

sentences.en: So how does this changing the channel thing go?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想并不像他们希望的那样好。

sentences.en: You know, like, not as great as they would have hoped, I imagine.
sentences.zh: 活动团体和民选官员之间有很多关于如何看待这件事的讨论。

sentences.en: There is a lot of talk among activist groups and among elected officials just about what to make of it.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州的一个投票权组织联盟计划抵制拜登总统今天在亚特兰大的演讲。

sentences.en: A coalition of voting rights groups in Georgia are planning to boycott President Biden's speech today in Atlanta.
sentences.zh: 在演讲当天，很明显有些团体就是不买账。

sentences.en: On the day of the speech, it becomes clear that some groups just won't stand for it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们宁愿总统留在华盛顿，

sentences.en: You know, we'd rather that the president stayed in D.C.
sentences.zh: 或许向参议院、向民主党核心小组发表这次演讲。

sentences.en: and perhaps delivered this speech to the
sentences.zh: 他们会见了他。

sentences.en: Senate, to the Democratic caucus.
sentences.zh: “黑人选民至上”组织的克里夫·奥尔布赖特称这只是作秀。

sentences.en: They meet him.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，我们不需要另一场演讲。

sentences.en: You had Cliff Albright of Black Voters Matter call it a photo op.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要他来佐治亚州把我们当作道具。

sentences.en: At this point, we don't need another speech.
sentences.zh: 我们需要的是行动。

sentences.en: We don't need him to come to Georgia and use us as a prop.
sentences.zh: 我们需要的是工作。

sentences.en: What we need is work.
sentences.zh: 我们需要的是工作。

sentences.en: Stacey Abrams, who is running again for governor of Georgia and is certainly the most notable
sentences.zh: 斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯（Stacey Abrams）再次竞选佐治亚州州长，她无疑是该州最受瞩目的民主党人，她提到了日程冲突的问题。

sentences.en: Democrat in that state, cited the scheduling conflict.
sentences.zh: 该州最受瞩目的民主党人，她提到了日程冲突的问题。

sentences.en: I spoke with Stacey this morning.
sentences.zh: 我今天早上和斯泰西通过话。

sentences.en: We have a great relationship.
sentences.zh: 我们的关系很好。

sentences.en: We got our scheduling mixed up.
sentences.zh: 我们的日程安排搞混了。

sentences.en: I'm going to be, I talked for their length this morning.
sentences.zh: 我打算……我今天早上和他们谈了很久。

sentences.en: We're all on the same page and everything's fine.
sentences.zh: 我们意见一致，一切都好。

sentences.en: But, you know, most people can make room for the president if they would like to, you know?
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，大多数人如果愿意的话，是可以为总统腾出时间的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so I think the general feeling, even before Biden even said something, was this was a sign of the fissures that have now come on voting rights.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，甚至在拜登开口之前，普遍的感觉就是，这标志着投票权问题上已经出现了裂痕。

sentences.en: These groups are already, frankly, rather exhausted, even before the president started to talk.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这些团体在总统开始讲话之前就已经相当疲惫了。

sentences.en: And just to explain, what are they exhausted of?
sentences.zh: 解释一下，他们对什么感到疲惫？

sentences.en: They're exhausted of the fact that voting rights is a capstone rather than a starting point for this presidency?
sentences.zh: 他们是否对“投票权”只是本届政府的收官之作，而非起点感到疲惫？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, they are asking the White House to solve an unsolvable problem, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种程度上，他们是在要求白宫解决一个无法解决的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: We know that the consistent block to those bills happening is the Senate filibuster and the rules that don't allow most things to pass without a 60-person vote.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，阻碍这些法案通过的一贯障碍是参议院的阻挠议事（filibuster），以及那些不允许大多数事项在没有60票支持下通过的规则。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that has hamstrung Democrats time and time and time again, and is doing so now.
sentences.zh: 这已经一次又一次地束缚了民主党人，现在依然如此。

sentences.en: And so on voting rights, you really have this activist in Georgia saying, spare Georgians your speech.
sentences.zh: 所以在投票权问题上，你确实看到佐治亚州的活动人士在说：别再对佐治亚人发表讲话了。

sentences.en: Spare coming here for that backdrop, because this is really a question of just how much individual pressure we put on Manchin in West Virginia, on Sinema in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 别再为了那种背景而来到这里，因为这实际上是一个关于我们对西弗吉尼亚州的曼钦和亚利桑那州的西内马施加多少个人压力的问题。

sentences.en: And that is, frankly, an insider DC question now.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这现在是一个华盛顿特区的内部问题。

sentences.en: It is not actually a public support-driven problem.
sentences.zh: 这实际上并不是一个由公众支持驱动的问题。

sentences.en: They said that they've done their jobs, and their frustration is that they feel that the White House and Democratic officials in Congress
sentences.zh: 他们说他们已经尽职尽责了，他们的挫败感在于，他们觉得白宫和国会的民主党官员

sentences.en: have not done theirs, which is to change the rules to make it happen.
sentences.zh: 没有尽到他们的职责，即修改规则以促成此事。

sentences.en: And they want the White House to take ownership of the fact that they have to make this happen.
sentences.zh: 他们希望白宫承担起责任，承认他们必须促成此事。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So the reason these activists are snubbing President Biden when he comes to Georgia
sentences.zh: 所以这些活动人士之所以在拜登总统来到佐治亚州发表关于投票权的演讲时冷落他，

sentences.en: to give a speech about voting rights is because, in their minds, it's like, why are you giving this speech to us?
sentences.zh: 是因为在他们看来，他们会想：你为什么要对我们发表这番演讲？

sentences.en: This is a speech that needs to be delivered to two United States senators, Joe Manchin
sentences.zh: 这番话应该对两位美国参议员说，乔·曼钦

sentences.en: and Kyrsten Sinema, who are opposed to getting rid of the filibuster in order to pass voting rights legislation.
sentences.zh: 和克里斯滕·西内马，他们反对废除阻挠议事以通过投票权立法。

sentences.en: So their message to Biden is, that's your problem.
sentences.zh: 所以他们给拜登的信息是：那是你的问题。

sentences.en: You sort it out.
sentences.zh: 你自己解决吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, this isn't just happening in isolation, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这并非孤立事件，对吧？

sentences.en: These are many of the same activists who were pushing Joe Biden from day one to take on the issue of voting rights directly.
sentences.zh: 这些活动人士中，有许多人从第一天起就一直在推动乔·拜登直接处理投票权问题。

sentences.en: And so their frustration is not actually because they disagree with where the White House has arrived, or even the words that Joe Biden said in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的挫败感其实并不是因为他们不同意白宫目前的立场，甚至也不是因为乔·拜登在佐治亚州所说的话。

sentences.en: But really, they think that they did not move urgently enough.
sentences.zh: 而是他们真的认为白宫行动不够迅速。

sentences.en: And that's a feeling they have had for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉他们已经持续很久了。

sentences.en: But...
sentences.zh: 但是……

sentences.en: In our lives, in the lives of our nation, life of our nation...
sentences.zh: 在我们的一生中，在我们国家的一生中，我们国家的一生……

sentences.en: He gives the speech anyway.
sentences.zh: 他还是发表了演讲。

sentences.en: There are moments so stark that they divide all that came before and everything that followed.
sentences.zh: 有些时刻如此鲜明，以至于将过去的一切与随之而来的一切分割开来。

sentences.en: And in terms of words, and in terms of rhetoric, it is the speech that activists have been asking for
sentences.zh: 就言辞和修辞而言，这就是活动人士多年来一直要求

sentences.en: Joe Biden to give for years.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登发表的演讲。

sentences.en: Hear me plainly.
sentences.zh: 听清楚了。

sentences.en: The battle for the soul of America is not over.
sentences.zh: 捍卫美国灵魂的战斗尚未结束。

sentences.en: We must stand strong and stand together to make sure January 6th marks not the end of democracy, but the beginning, a renaissance of our democracy.
sentences.zh: 我们必须坚定立场，团结一致，确保1月6日标志着的不是民主的终结，而是开始，是我们民主的复兴。

sentences.en: I mean, he frames this as a must-pass bills for the state of democracy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他将此定性为民主国家必须通过的法案。

sentences.en: Jim Crow 2.0 is about two insidious things.
sentences.zh: “吉姆·克劳2.0”涉及两件阴险的事情。

sentences.en: Voter suppression and election subversion.
sentences.zh: 压制选民和颠覆选举。

sentences.en: He talks about election subversion, a thing that goes beyond just voter suppression and the fears that votes will not be counted properly or they will be disregarded.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了颠覆选举，这不仅仅是压制选民，还包括对选票无法被正确统计或被无视的担忧。

sentences.en: It's about who gets to count the vote and whether your vote counts at all.
sentences.zh: 这关乎谁有权统计选票，以及你的选票是否真的有效。

sentences.en: Which is certainly a growing concern coming out of 2020 and something he hasn't really talked about.
sentences.zh: 这无疑是2020年大选后日益增长的担忧，也是他之前并未真正谈论过的问题。

sentences.en: Today, I'm making it clear, to protect our democracy, I support changing the Senate rules.
sentences.zh: 今天，我明确表示，为了保护我们的民主，我支持修改参议院规则。

sentences.en: Whichever way they need to be changed.
sentences.zh: 无论需要以何种方式修改。

sentences.en: He explicitly endorses ending the Senate filibuster on the issue of voting rights.
sentences.zh: 他明确支持在投票权问题上终结参议院的阻挠议事。

sentences.en: So I ask every elected official in America, how do you want to be remembered?
sentences.zh: 所以我问美国每一位民选官员：你们希望被后人如何铭记？

sentences.en: He frames it really morally in the legacy of the great racial fights of American history.
sentences.zh: 他确实从道德层面将其置于美国历史上伟大的种族斗争的遗产中。

sentences.en: At consequential moments in history, they present a choice.
sentences.zh: 在历史的关键时刻，人们面临着选择。

sentences.en: Do you want to be on the side of Dr. King or George Wallace?
sentences.zh: 你想站在马丁·路德·金博士一边，还是乔治·华莱士一边？

sentences.en: Do you want to be on the side of John Lewis or Bull Connor?
sentences.zh: 你想站在约翰·刘易斯一边，还是布尔·康纳一边？

sentences.en: Saying that frankly people have a choice about whether they want to be on the side of Bull Connor
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这是在说人们可以选择站在布尔·康纳一边，

sentences.en: and other notorious racists or on the sides of John Lewis and civil rights activists.
sentences.zh: 还是站在其他臭名昭著的种族主义者一边，亦或是站在约翰·刘易斯和民权活动人士一边。

sentences.en: This is the moment to decide, to defend our elections, to defend our democracy.
sentences.zh: 现在是决定捍卫我们选举、捍卫我们民主的时刻了。

sentences.en: It's really a kind of like classic example of the bully pulpit we read about in government class in high school.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我们高中政府课上读到的“讲坛政治”（bully pulpit）的经典例子。

sentences.en: May God bless you all and may God protect the sacred right to vote.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝保佑你们所有人，愿上帝保护神圣的投票权。

sentences.en: This is a president knowing that what he can command is media attention and interest, going to a place to make that even more dramatic,
sentences.zh: 这是一位总统深知自己能掌控的是媒体的关注和兴趣，他前往某个地方让这种关注变得更加戏剧化，

sentences.en: and laying out the stakes for this upcoming political fight in hopes of rallying pressure around the Senate holdouts.
sentences.zh: 并为即将到来的政治斗争设定赌注，希望能围绕参议院的阻挠者施加压力。

sentences.en: But by the end of the week, it had become clear that the moral play that he was making, that the bully pulpit he was seeking to use,
sentences.zh: 但到了周末，很明显，他所采取的道德姿态，他试图利用的“讲坛政治”，

sentences.en: the influence and pressure he was hoping to have, was falling flat.
sentences.zh: 他所希望产生的影响力和压力，都落空了。

sentences.en: And frankly, voting rights was no closer to passing the day before this speech than the day after.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，投票权法案在演讲前后的通过可能性并没有什么区别。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall, to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间跨越付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: — So instead, let's pick up where we left off.
sentences.zh: ——那么，让我们接着刚才的话题继续。

sentences.en: President Biden has asked Democrats to eliminate the filibuster so that he can pass these voting rights bills,
sentences.zh: 拜登总统已要求民主党人取消阻挠议事，以便他能通过这些投票权法案，

sentences.en: and told them basically, if you don't, you're going to be on the wrong side of history.
sentences.zh: 并基本上告诉他们：如果不这样做，你们将站在历史错误的一边。

sentences.en: So, what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: — Well, the speech was the first step of a week of full-court press on the White House's part.
sentences.zh: ——嗯，这次演讲是白宫方面为期一周全面施压的第一步。

sentences.en: And the next step was Biden physically going to Capitol Hill to make the pitch he made in Georgia in person.
sentences.zh: 下一步是拜登亲自前往国会山，当面推销他在佐治亚州提出的主张。

sentences.en: — Which is rare, by the way.
sentences.zh: ——顺便说一句，这很罕见。

sentences.en: Presidents don't normally go to the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 总统通常不会去国会大厦。

sentences.en: Usually the Capitol comes to the Presidents.
sentences.zh: 通常是国会大厦的人来见总统。

sentences.en: — Absolutely.
sentences.zh: ——绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It is an intentional show of political force.
sentences.zh: 这是一种故意的政治力量展示。

sentences.en: It's intentional use of political capital.
sentences.zh: 这是对政治资本的刻意使用。

sentences.en: It's basically the White House doing what those activists in Georgia said they should do, which is take that speech and give it to the people who are on the Hill.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是白宫在做那些佐治亚州活动人士说他们应该做的事，即把演讲内容带给国会山的人。

sentences.en: The problem is...
sentences.zh: 问题是……

sentences.en: — Mr. President.
sentences.zh: ——总统先生。

sentences.en: — The senator from Arizona.
sentences.zh: ——来自亚利桑那州的参议员。

sentences.en: — Even as the president is arriving to make that concerted pitch, the relevant Democrats made clear to him that they weren't really receptive or listening.
sentences.zh: ——即使总统亲自前来进行那次协调一致的推销，相关的民主党人也向他明确表示，他们并不怎么接受或听取意见。

sentences.en: — I rise at a challenging, divisive time for our nation.
sentences.zh: ——我在我们国家充满挑战和分裂的时刻站在这里。

sentences.en: For years...
sentences.zh: 多年来……

sentences.en: — You had Senator Kyrsten Sinema of Arizona give what was, in my opinion, a surprisingly direct speech about her opposition to the filibuster.
sentences.zh: ——亚利桑那州参议员克里斯滕·西内马发表了在我看来令人惊讶的直接演讲，表达了她对阻挠议事的反对。

sentences.en: — While I continue to support these bills, I will not support separate actions that worsen the underlying disease of division infecting our country.
sentences.zh: ——虽然我继续支持这些法案，但我不会支持那些加剧感染我们国家的潜在分裂疾病的单独行动。

sentences.en: — Both reinforcing that that position is unchanged and really throwing cold water on this political moment that the White House was trying to create.
sentences.zh: ——这既重申了她的立场没有改变，也确实给白宫试图营造的政治氛围泼了一盆冷水。

sentences.en: — We must address the disease itself, the disease of division, to protect our democracy.
sentences.zh: ——我们必须解决疾病本身，即分裂的疾病，以保护我们的民主。

sentences.en: And it cannot be achieved by one party alone.
sentences.zh: 而且这不能仅靠一个政党来实现。

sentences.en: — She is standing in the most public place you can on Capitol Hill, saying that the very thing that the president is there to try to do is a non-starter.
sentences.zh: ——她站在国会山最公开的地方，说总统此行的目的根本行不通。

sentences.en: — We have but one democracy.
sentences.zh: ——我们只有一个民主国家。

sentences.en: We can only survive.
sentences.zh: 我们只能生存下去。

sentences.en: We can only keep her if we do so together.
sentences.zh: 只有团结一致，我们才能守护她。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: — And so, here you have the president, on the same day in which he comes to the Capitol to make that political investment, really have a kind of public embarrassment with Sinema,
sentences.zh: ——所以，总统在前往国会山进行政治投入的同一天，却在西内马那里遭遇了公开的尴尬，

sentences.en: and later that same day with Joe Manchin of West Virginia, who released a statement saying he was also opposed to changes in the filibuster, a position he's held for a while.
sentences.zh: 当天晚些时候，西弗吉尼亚州的乔·曼钦也发表声明称，他同样反对修改阻挠议事，这一立场他已经坚持了一段时间。

sentences.en: He reiterated it on that same day.
sentences.zh: 他在同一天重申了这一点。

sentences.en: I think this is not only Biden taking a hit in a political sense, but taking it in a kind of public way.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不仅是拜登在政治意义上受挫，而且是以一种公开的方式受挫。

sentences.en: The key point of his agenda is dying before his eyes here at the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 他议程的核心部分正在国会大厦这里眼睁睁地死去。

sentences.en: — Right.
sentences.zh: ——没错。

sentences.en: Because what they're saying is, we refuse to change the filibuster, which is the equivalent of saying your voting rights bills are dead.
sentences.zh: 因为他们说的是：我们拒绝修改阻挠议事，这等同于说你们的投票权法案已经死了。

sentences.en: — It means your voting rights bill is dead.
sentences.zh: ——这意味着你的投票权法案已经死了。

sentences.en: It means your gun reform bill is dead.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你的枪支改革法案已经死了。

sentences.en: It means that everything is dead that either doesn't specifically appeal to Republicans or doesn't fit that narrow budget definition of something that relates to the economy.
sentences.zh: 这意味着所有那些既不能特别吸引共和党人，又不符合预算和解程序中关于经济定义的法案都死了。

sentences.en: It can therefore go through budget reconciliation and only require 50 votes.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们可以通过预算和解程序，只需50票即可通过。

sentences.en: That means so many of the agenda items that Democrats have really promised to people as a baseline are probably not going to be addressed in this current environment.
sentences.zh: 这意味着民主党人向民众承诺的许多基本议程项目，在当前环境下可能都无法得到解决。

sentences.en: I mean, voting rights is the tip of the spear, but we're really talking about what is the larger Democratic agenda.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，投票权只是冰山一角，但我们实际上是在讨论更大的民主党议程是什么。

sentences.en: And it's a real blow to the overall strategy, too, right?
sentences.zh: 这对整体战略也是一个沉重的打击，对吧？

sentences.en: The reason you do the speech, the reason you make the public moral play on this issue is in the hopes that Sinema and Manchin see that public pressure and cave,
sentences.zh: 你发表演讲、在这个问题上进行公开道德博弈的原因，是希望西内马和曼钦看到这种公众压力后会屈服，

sentences.en: or at least seem open or have a renewed openness to the discussion.
sentences.zh: 或者至少表现出开放态度，或者对讨论重新产生开放性。

sentences.en: But when you have a senator who's willing to go and make such a public statement against it, it is not only a legislative blow, as we said,
sentences.zh: 但当有一位参议员愿意站出来发表如此公开的反对声明时，这不仅如我们所说是一次立法上的打击，

sentences.en: but it just means that that shame tactic, that pressure tactic, isn't really working.
sentences.zh: 而且意味着那种羞辱策略、那种压力策略并没有真正奏效。

sentences.en: But instead, surely President Biden knew that this was how it was going to play out, right?
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，拜登总统肯定知道事情会这样发展，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe not in the particular way it played out with two members of his own party essentially embarrassing him so publicly on the Hill,
sentences.zh: 也许他没料到会以这种特定的方式发生，即他自己党内的两名成员在国会山上如此公开地让他难堪，

sentences.en: but he had to know that Senators Sinema and Manchin would not change their position on ending the filibuster.
sentences.zh: 但他肯定知道参议员西内马和曼钦不会改变他们关于终结阻挠议事的立场。

sentences.en: They've been consistent about this.
sentences.zh: 他们在这方面一直很坚定。

sentences.en: And so why then so publicly call for something that isn't going to happen, especially given the implications you just outlined,
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么还要如此公开地呼吁一件注定不会发生的事情呢？尤其是考虑到你刚才概述的后果，

sentences.en: which is that it not happening is very consequential in a bad way for the entire rest of the presidency?
sentences.zh: 即这件事不发生对整个剩余任期来说后果非常严重？

sentences.en: Because it's the only play that was really left.
sentences.zh: 因为这是唯一剩下的招数了。

sentences.en: He knows that these are people who have independent political power in their states.
sentences.zh: 他知道这些人各自在自己的州拥有独立的政治权力。

sentences.en: He knows that these are headstrong folks.
sentences.zh: 他知道这些人很固执。

sentences.en: And he knows Manchin and Sinema.
sentences.zh: 他也了解曼钦和西内马。

sentences.en: But he also is dealing with competing pressures, as we talked about, from activist groups, from organizers, and from a public
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所讨论的，他还要应对来自活动团体、组织者以及公众的竞争性压力，

sentences.en: that wants to see that they understand the urgency of the issue, even if they cannot get the things done.
sentences.zh: 公众希望看到他们理解问题的紧迫性，即使他们无法完成这些事情。

sentences.en: And so what we essentially see the White House saying is that saying something, even if you can't do anything, is better than saying nothing and not doing anything.
sentences.zh: 所以我们本质上看到白宫在说：说点什么，即使你什么也做不了，也比什么都不说、什么都不做要好。

sentences.en: You know, that when you go to Georgia, they are going to be as explicit as possible in hopes, frankly, that the public and that the midterm voters
sentences.zh: 你知道，当他们去佐治亚州时，他们会尽可能明确地表达立场，坦率地说，是希望公众和中期选举的选民

sentences.en: give them effort points, give them...
sentences.zh: 能给他们“努力分”，给他们……

sentences.en: Effort points.
sentences.zh: 努力分。

sentences.en: Yeah, give them an A for effort.
sentences.zh: 是的，给他们一个努力的A。

sentences.en: They want to shift the blame, is probably the best way to say it.
sentences.zh: 他们想转移责任，这可能是最好的说法。

sentences.en: And so that a voter can still feel good about the Biden presidency, even with the agenda items that were supposed to come from the Biden presidency have not come, right?
sentences.zh: 这样选民仍然可以对拜登政府感觉良好，即使那些本应来自拜登政府的议程项目并没有实现，对吧？

sentences.en: So the way the White House is positing doing that is making clear that it was not because they don't want those things,
sentences.zh: 所以白宫提出这样做的方式是明确表示，这并不是因为他们不想要这些东西，

sentences.en: but these individual senators are blocking them from doing those things.
sentences.zh: 而是这些个别参议员在阻碍他们实现这些目标。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we may be failing here, but we're going to fail trying.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这里可能会失败，但我们会努力尝试。

sentences.en: And communicating that trying and that urgency,
sentences.zh: 而传达出那种尝试和紧迫感，

sentences.en: that's important to the White House at this moment.
sentences.zh: 这对白宫来说在当下非常重要。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that we should be clear because look at the political context.
sentences.zh: 而且我们应该明确这一点，因为看看当前的政治背景吧。

sentences.en: They have entered now into an election year where Democrats are already facing an uphill climb in the midterm elections, and they are going to need the energy of their base, right?
sentences.zh: 他们现在已经进入了选举年，民主党人在中期选举中已经面临艰难的爬坡，他们将需要其选民基础的能量，对吧？

sentences.en: You're starting to hear more and more Democrats say that they need to show the voters that they are trying.
sentences.zh: 你开始听到越来越多的民主党人说，他们需要向选民展示他们正在努力。

sentences.en: That really only works, though, for a baseline Democrat, for someone who already likes you, for someone who is already inclined to vote for you.
sentences.zh: 然而，这实际上只对核心民主党人有效，对那些已经喜欢你、已经倾向于投票给你的人才有效。

sentences.en: Where Democrats think that they have to go, though, the voter that they need is a marginal voter, is someone who often sits out the midterms,
sentences.zh: 但民主党人认为他们必须去争取的选民，是那些边缘选民，是那些经常不参加中期选举的人，

sentences.en: is a young person, is someone who is not college educated, is someone who is outside of the sphere of people who are already their baseline set of voters who come out.
sentences.zh: 是年轻人，是没有受过大学教育的人，是那些已经在他们核心选民圈子之外的人。

sentences.en: And the problem is, you talk to any kind of consultant, political person, organizer, I have never heard anyone say that that type of marginal voter
sentences.zh: 问题在于，你和任何顾问、政治人物、组织者交谈，我从未听过任何人说那种边缘选民

sentences.en: is moved by the effort points, right?
sentences.zh: 会被“努力分”所打动，对吧？

sentences.en: Those are the type of people who specifically want things that touch them, who are removed from the political process,
sentences.zh: 这些人特别想要的是与他们切身相关的东西，他们远离政治进程，

sentences.en: who really the word filibuster is a word from another planet, right?
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，“阻挠议事”这个词简直就像来自另一个星球，对吧？

sentences.en: Those are the type of voters who have to be motivated.
sentences.zh: 这些类型的选民必须被激励起来。

sentences.en: And explain to that person why it's a senator's fault and not the president's fault is a lot harder of a task.
sentences.zh: 向那个人解释为什么这是参议员的错而不是总统的错，是一项艰巨得多的任务。

sentences.en: Because frankly, you all got these next to your name, you know?
sentences.zh: 因为坦白说，你们的名字旁边都有这些标签，你懂的？

sentences.en: Like, it's the open question of whether that type of person is looking at a speech in Georgia and absolving the president of guilt.
sentences.zh: 比如，这类人是否在看乔治亚州的演讲时会免除总统的责任，这还是个未解的问题。

sentences.en: If that answer is no, if they didn't look at the speech in Georgia, if they don't care about the distinctions between Senator Manchin,
sentences.zh: 如果答案是否定的，如果他们没看乔治亚州的演讲，如果他们不在乎曼钦参议员之间的区别，

sentences.en: if they're not absolving blame because of the filibuster, then yeah, not delivering on voting rights is a problem.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没有因为“阻挠议事”而免除（总统的）责任，那么是的，在投票权问题上没有兑现承诺就是一个问题。

sentences.en: So that leaves Biden, on an issue like voting rights, is speaking to a pretty narrow band of Democratic voters, the base, the people who would care about effort points.
sentences.zh: 所以这使得拜登在投票权这类问题上，只能与一小部分民主党选民对话，也就是基本盘，那些会在意“努力分”的人。

sentences.en: And it would leave him less effectively speaking to those people you just mentioned, the people who want deliverables and aren't that ideological
sentences.zh: 这会让他无法有效地与你刚才提到的那些人对话，即那些想要实际成果、不太讲究意识形态、

sentences.en: and aren't that obsessed with politics.
sentences.zh: 也不那么沉迷于政治的人。

sentences.en: And it seems like you need all those voters to show up if you're a Democratic president trying to keep control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一位试图在即将到来的中期选举中保持国会控制权的民主党总统，看起来你需要所有这些选民都出来投票。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: For Democrats to succeed, it is pretty universally agreed that they need to do all of the above and not passing voting rights makes that more difficult.
sentences.zh: 对于民主党人来说，要取得成功，人们普遍认为他们需要做到上述所有事情，而未能通过投票权法案让这变得更加困难。

sentences.en: It also has another effect, kind of irrespective of messaging, which is that it is the gateway to how power functions.
sentences.zh: 这还有另一个影响，某种程度上与信息传递无关，那就是它是权力运作的门户。

sentences.en: And so in Democrats' own language, these bills are a little more important than the other ones.
sentences.zh: 因此，用民主党自己的话来说，这些法案比其他法案稍微重要一些。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because, you know, Eric Holder, the former attorney general, told me that he sees it as we might not have fair elections if these bills don't pass in the future.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，前司法部长埃里克·霍尔德告诉我，他认为如果这些法案将来不能通过，我们可能就不会有公平的选举了。

sentences.en: And so if those are the stakes, there's not just a political impact to individually not passing these bills and the type of people who are disappointed.
sentences.zh: 所以如果赌注是这样，那么未能通过这些法案不仅会对个人产生政治影响，也会让那些人感到失望。

sentences.en: But we're talking about a party impact of how do Democrats ensure that they have representation across the country.
sentences.zh: 但我们谈论的是对政党的影响，即民主党如何确保他们在全国范围内拥有代表权。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because if Democrats are to be believed about why these bills need to be passed in the first place,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们要相信民主党人关于为什么首先需要通过这些法案的说法，

sentences.en: it's because there's a threat to the election system in the country.
sentences.zh: 那是因为国家的选举制度受到了威胁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And candidly, they would say a threat to them more than to anybody else.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，他们会说这对他们的威胁比对任何人都大。

sentences.en: And so not passing these bills is not just a political problem for Democrats, right?
sentences.zh: 所以未能通过这些法案不仅仅是民主党人的政治问题，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like a mechanical problem in their ability, they would argue, to actually get votes counted and get election victories certified.
sentences.zh: 他们会认为，这就像是他们在实际统计选票和认证选举胜利能力上的一个机械性问题。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And for a lot of people across the country, it is like put up or shut up time about the threat.
sentences.zh: 对于全国许多人来说，现在是时候就这种威胁拿出行动，否则就闭嘴了。

sentences.en: You know, the folks who are looking at Biden, the people who skipped that speech, really what they are saying is that they want a Democratic Party
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些看着拜登的人，那些跳过那次演讲的人，他们真正想说的是，他们想要一个民主党，

sentences.en: that is putting as much effort into the solution as they are into the description of the problem.
sentences.zh: 一个在解决问题上投入的精力与描述问题时一样多的民主党。

sentences.en: And for a lot of the organizers and activists, they really feel like these politicians are coming to their communities over and over to tell them about a threat
sentences.zh: 对于许多组织者和活动家来说，他们真的觉得这些政客一次又一次地来到他们的社区，告诉他们一个他们早就知道的威胁，

sentences.en: that they already know, right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like that they've lived with, not in the last 10 years, but in the history of this country.
sentences.zh: 就像他们不仅在过去10年里，而是在这个国家的历史上一直生活在其中一样。

sentences.en: You ain't got to tell Georgia about voting rights, right?
sentences.zh: 你不需要告诉乔治亚州关于投票权的事，对吧？

sentences.en: These people feel that it is about follow through.
sentences.zh: 这些人觉得关键在于后续行动。

sentences.en: So at the end of the day,
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，

sentences.en: will a failure to pass voting rights be better or worse than never having called for and carried out a debate and voted on it at all?
sentences.zh: 未能通过投票权法案，会比根本没有发起、进行辩论并进行投票更好还是更坏？

sentences.en: Well, we've talked about the challenges to really motivating people in the short term on trying and effort.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们已经讨论过在短期内通过尝试和努力来真正激励人们所面临的挑战。

sentences.en: But I really think this is a long-term question.
sentences.zh: 但我真的认为这是一个长期的问题。

sentences.en: The stakes of voting rights as described by the Democratic Party are no less than the democracy itself, right?
sentences.zh: 正如民主党所描述的那样，投票权的赌注不亚于民主本身，对吧？

sentences.en: These bills are supposed to be the thin line between fair and honest elections and not against an ongoing Republican threat.
sentences.zh: 这些法案本应是公平诚实的选举与持续的共和党威胁之间的一道防线。

sentences.en: If Democrats are right and the failure to pass these bills changes how we have to think about elections in the future, changes the fairness question, I don't think credit

sentences.en: in the short term of this midterms will be what people remember.
sentences.zh: 人们会记得这些功劳。

sentences.en: I really think it will be about blame.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为人们会记得的是指责。

sentences.en: I think people will look back at a window of action and wonder who was asleep at the wheel.
sentences.zh: 我想人们会回顾那段行动窗口期，想知道是谁在关键时刻睡着了。
